RESOLVE App

Source: vignettes/articles/app.Rmd
app.Rmd

Impute the habitat (EUNIS), site metadata (altitude, slope, location) and survey metadata (plot area, survey year) of vegetation plots from their species composition and cover-abundance, with the released RESOLVE models trained on the plots of the European Vegetation Archive (EVA). The models run locally in your browser; your files are not uploaded. The page downloads the models and the elevation model from Zenodo (models, elevation model), the map from OpenStreetMap and, for a map download, the country boundaries from Eurostat GISCO.

Plots

    Imputed values

          Each variable is imputed by five models, trained in the same way from different random starting points (seeds), and the page combines their five values: habitat by majority vote (seed agreement is the share of the five naming the habitat), numeric variables by their mean and standard deviation, and location by the spherical mean and the median distance of the five from it.

          Altitude and slope can also be corrected with an elevation model (Copernicus GLO-30). The correction weighs the imputed value against the elevation model's value at the plot and over the square kilometre around it, depending on the plot's location uncertainty, the spread of the five values and how many of the plot's species the models know. The table gives the elevation model's own values beside the corrected ones.
